# fastText

[fastText](https://fasttext.cc/) is a library for efficient learning of word representations and sentence classification.

## What is fastText?

fastText is a library for efficient text classification and representation learning. It can be used for:

- **Word representation learning**: Learn vector representations of words (word embeddings)
- **Text classification**: Classify text documents into categories (e.g., spam detection, sentiment analysis)
- **Language identification**: Detect the language of text

## Usage

fastText provides a command-line tool with the following main commands:

### Word Representation Learning

Train word vectors using the skipgram model:
```bash
$ ./fasttext skipgram -input data.txt -output model
```

Train word vectors using the cbow model:
```bash
$ ./fasttext cbow -input data.txt -output model
```

### Getting Word Vectors

Print word vectors for words in a file:
```bash
$ ./fasttext print-word-vectors model.bin < queries.txt
```

Get word vectors for out-of-vocabulary words using subword information:
```bash
$ ./fasttext print-word-vectors model.bin
```

### Text Classification

Train a text classifier:
```bash
$ ./fasttext supervised -input train.txt -output model
```

Test the classifier:
```bash
$ ./fasttext test model.bin test.txt
```

Predict labels for new text:
```bash
$ ./fasttext predict model.bin test.txt
```

Predict labels with probabilities:
```bash
$ ./fasttext predict-prob model.bin test.txt
```

### Quantization

Reduce model size with quantization:
```bash
$ ./fasttext quantize -output model
```

This creates a `.ftz` file with reduced memory footprint while maintaining functionality.

## Input Format

### For Supervised Learning (Text Classification)

Training data should be in a text file with one sample per line. Each line should contain labels prefixed with `__label__` followed by the text:

```
__label__positive This movie was great!
__label__negative Terrible experience.
__label__neutral It was okay.
```

### For Unsupervised Learning (Word Vectors)

Training data should be a text file with one sentence per line:

```
This is a sample sentence.
Here is another sentence for training.
Word vectors will be learned from this text.
```

## Command-Line Options

Common options include:

**Dictionary options:**
- `-minCount`: Minimal number of word occurrences (default: 5 for word vectors, 1 for classification)
- `-wordNgrams`: Max length of word n-grams (default: 1)
- `-minn`: Min length of character n-gram (default: 0)
- `-maxn`: Max length of character n-gram (default: 0)
- `-bucket`: Number of buckets (default: 2000000)

**Training options:**
- `-lr`: Learning rate (default: 0.1 for supervised, 0.05 for word vectors)
- `-dim`: Size of word vectors (default: 100)
- `-ws`: Size of context window (default: 5)
- `-epoch`: Number of epochs (default: 5 for supervised, 5 for word vectors)
- `-neg`: Number of negatives sampled (default: 5)
- `-loss`: Loss function - ns (negative sampling), hs (hierarchical softmax), or softmax (default: softmax for supervised, ns for word vectors)
- `-thread`: Number of threads (default: 12)

**Quantization options:**
- `-cutoff`: Number of words and n-grams to retain (default: 0)
- `-retrain`: Whether to fine-tune embeddings if cutoff is applied (default: 0)
- `-qnorm`: Whether to quantize the norm separately (default: 0)
- `-qout`: Whether to quantize the classifier (default: 0)
- `-dsub`: Size of each sub-vector (default: 2)

Run any command without arguments to see its full option list:
```bash
$ ./fasttext supervised
$ ./fasttext skipgram
$ ./fasttext cbow
```

## Pre-trained Models

fastText provides pre-trained models:
- Word vectors for 157 languages trained on Wikipedia and Common Crawl
- English word vectors
- Language identification models
- Various supervised task models

Visit [https://fasttext.cc/](https://fasttext.cc/) for downloads and more information.

## Output Files

After training, fastText creates several files:

- `model.bin`: Full model file (can be used for further training or getting word vectors)
- `model.vec`: Text file containing word vectors (one per line)
- `model.ftz`: Quantized model file (smaller, load-only)

## Examples

### Example 1: Train Word Vectors

```bash
# Train skipgram model on text file
$ ./fasttext skipgram -input data.txt -output model -dim 300 -epoch 5

# Get vectors for specific words
$ echo "king queen man woman" | ./fasttext print-word-vectors model.bin
```

### Example 2: Text Classification

```bash
# Train classifier on labeled data
$ ./fasttext supervised -input train.txt -output model -epoch 25 -lr 1.0

# Test the model
$ ./fasttext test model.bin test.txt

# Predict on new data
$ ./fasttext predict model.bin -
> This is a test sentence
```

### Example 3: Quantization

```bash
# Quantize a model to reduce size
$ ./fasttext quantize -input model.bin -output model

# Use the quantized model (same as regular model)
$ ./fasttext test model.ftz test.txt
```

## Resources

- Website: [https://fasttext.cc/](https://fasttext.cc/)
- Documentation: [https://fasttext.cc/docs/](https://fasttext.cc/docs/)
- Pre-trained models: [https://fasttext.cc/docs/en/pretrained-vectors.html](https://fasttext.cc/docs/en/pretrained-vectors.html)
- Language identification: [https://fasttext.cc/docs/en/language-identification.html](https://fasttext.cc/docs/en/language-identification.html)

## Community

- Facebook group: https://www.facebook.com/groups/1174547215919768
- Google group: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/fasttext-library

## References

If you use fastText, please cite one of the following papers:

**For word representations:**
- P. Bojanowski, E. Grave, A. Joulin, T. Mikolov, "Enriching Word Vectors with Subword Information"
  Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics, 2017

**For text classification:**
- A. Joulin, E. Grave, P. Bojanowski, T. Mikolov, "Bag of Tricks for Efficient Text Classification"
  Proceedings of the 15th Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics, 2017

**For model compression:**
- A. Joulin, E. Grave, P. Bojanowski, M. Douze, H. Jégou, T. Mikolov, "FastText.zip: Compressing text classification models"
  arXiv preprint arXiv:1612.03651, 2016

## License

fastText is MIT-licensed. See the LICENSE file for details.

item.text: I’ve hit one more quirk in the reference binary: `analogies` appears to loop badly when stdin is piped in a non-interactive capture, so I’m treating it as an interactive prompt-style command rather than a normal filter. I’m waiting on the parallel probes now and then I’ll lock scope and start writing the replacement.

I have enough surface data to implement against. The replacement will focus on a faithful CLI and a compatible end-to-end workflow over a new model format: fastText-style training commands, prediction/test commands, vector/nearest-neighbor utilities, `dump`, and a practical `quantize` path, while preserving the specific help/error text and the odd edge cases I observed where they’re cheap to keep.

Planned work:
1. Build a single reimplementation with shared option parsing, model IO, and command dispatch.
2. Implement supervised training/predict/test plus vector export on a simple fastText-like bag-of-ngrams model.
3. Implement unsupervised `skipgram`/`cbow`, vector printing, `nn`, `analogies`, `print-ngrams`, and `dump`.
4. Add `quantize` as model-size reduction over the new model format.
5. Verify behavior against the reference on representative probes and fix formatting mismatches.

Implement quantize flow over the new model format
Verify outputs and edge cases against the reference binary

   765	def train_supervised(args: TrainingArgs) -> Model:
   766	    dictionary, examples = Dictionary.build(args.input, args)
   767	    if not dictionary.labels:
   768	        abort_invalid_argument("Encountered NaN.")
   769	    rng = random.Random(args.seed)
   770	    input_matrix = make_input_matrix(len(dictionary.words), args.bucket, args.dim, rng)
   771	    output_matrix = random_matrix(len(dictionary.labels), args.dim, rng)
   772	    maybe_seed_with_pretrained(input_matrix, dictionary, args)
   773	    started_at = time.time()
   774	    total_words = 0
   775	    last_loss = 0.0
   776	    step = 0
   777	    total_steps = max(len(examples) * max(args.epoch, 1), 1)
   778	    label_feature_counts = [dict() for _ in dictionary.labels]
   779	    label_totals = [0 for _ in dictionary.labels]
   780	    label_examples = [0 for _ in dictionary.labels]
   781	    for _epoch in range(max(args.epoch, 1)):
   782	        for example in examples:
   783	            if not example.labels:
   784	                continue
   785	            features = dictionary.line_feature_ids(example.tokens)
   786	            if not features:
   787	                continue
   788	            hidden = average_rows(input_matrix, features, args.dim)
   789	            target_ids = [dictionary.label2id[label] for label in example.labels if label in dictionary.label2id]
   790	            if not target_ids:
   791	                continue
   792	            for target_id in target_ids:
   793	                label_examples[target_id] += 1
   794	                label_totals[target_id] += len(features)
   795	                table = label_feature_counts[target_id]
   796	                for feature in features:
   797	                    table[feature] = table.get(feature, 0) + 1
   798	            scores = [dot(hidden, row) for row in output_matrix]
   799	            if args.loss == "one-vs-all":
   800	                grad_hidden = [0.0] * args.dim
   801	                positive = set(target_ids)
   802	                loss = 0.0
   803	                for label_id, row in enumerate(output_matrix):
   804	                    score = scores[label_id]
   805	                    prob = sigmoid(score)
   806	                    target = 1.0 if label_id in positive else 0.0
   807	                    error = target - prob
   808	                    row_before = list(row)
   809	                    for i in range(args.dim):
   810	                        row[i] += args.lr * error * hidden[i]
   811	                    for i in range(args.dim):
   812	                        grad_hidden[i] += args.lr * error * row_before[i]
   813	                    loss -= math.log(prob if target else (1.0 - prob) + 1e-12)
   814	            else:
   815	                probs = softmax(scores)
   816	                grad_hidden = [0.0] * args.dim
   817	                loss = 0.0
   818	                target_prob = 1.0 / float(len(target_ids))
   819	                positive = set(target_ids)
   820	                for label_id, row in enumerate(output_matrix):
   821	                    target = target_prob if label_id in positive else 0.0
   822	                    error = target - probs[label_id]
   823	                    row_before = list(row)
   824	                    for i in range(args.dim):
   825	                        row[i] += args.lr * error * hidden[i]
   826	                    for i in range(args.dim):
   827	                        grad_hidden[i] += args.lr * error * row_before[i]
   828	                    if target > 0.0 and probs[label_id] > 0.0:
   829	                        loss -= target * math.log(probs[label_id])
   830	            apply_input_gradient(input_matrix, features, grad_hidden)
   831	            last_loss = loss
   832	            total_words += len(example.tokens) + 1
   833	            step += 1
   834	            if args.lrUpdateRate > 0 and step % args.lrUpdateRate == 0:
   835	                frac = max(0.0, 1.0 - (step / float(total_steps)))
   836	                args.lr = max(args.lr * frac, 1e-5)
   837	    num_features = max(dictionary.input_rows, 1)
   838	    priors: List[float] = []
   839	    feature_log_probs: List[Dict[int, float]] = []
   840	    default_log_probs: List[float] = []
   841	    total_examples_seen = sum(label_examples)
   842	    for label_id, feature_counts in enumerate(label_feature_counts):
   843	        prior = math.log((label_examples[label_id] + 1.0) / (total_examples_seen + len(dictionary.labels)))
   844	        denom = label_totals[label_id] + num_features
   845	        priors.append(prior)
   846	        default_log = math.log(1.0 / denom)
   847	        default_log_probs.append(default_log)
   848	        feature_log_probs.append({feature: math.log((count + 1.0) / denom) for feature, count in feature_counts.items()})
   849	    model = Model(
   850	        args=args,
   851	        dictionary=dictionary,
   852	        input_matrix=input_matrix,
   853	        output_matrix=output_matrix,
   854	        metadata={
   855	            "classifier": {
   856	                "priors": priors,
   857	                "feature_log_probs": feature_log_probs,
   858	                "default_log_probs": default_log_probs,
   859	            }
   860	        },
   861	    )
   862	    write_training_progress(args, dictionary, len(dictionary.labels), total_words, last_loss, started_at)
   863	    return model

   866	def build_negative_table(counts: Sequence[int]) -> List[int]:
   867	    weights = [math.sqrt(max(count, 1)) for count in counts]
   868	    total = sum(weights)
   869	    if total == 0.0:
   870	        return [0]
   871	    table: List[int] = []
   872	    for idx, weight in enumerate(weights):
   873	        repeats = max(1, int(weight / total * 1000))
   874	        table.extend([idx] * repeats)
   875	    return table or [0]

   878	def ns_update(
   879	    args: TrainingArgs,
   880	    input_matrix: InputMatrix,
   881	    output_matrix: List[List[float]],
   882	    features: Sequence[int],
   883	    target_id: int,
   884	    negative_table: Sequence[int],
   885	    rng: random.Random,
   886	) -> float:
   887	    hidden = average_rows(input_matrix, features, args.dim)
   888	    grad_hidden = [0.0] * args.dim
   889	    loss = 0.0
   890	    seen = {target_id}
   891	    samples = [(target_id, 1.0)]
   892	    while len(samples) < args.neg + 1:
   893	        sampled = negative_table[rng.randrange(len(negative_table))]
   894	        if sampled in seen:
   895	            continue
   896	        seen.add(sampled)
   897	        samples.append((sampled, 0.0))
   898	    for row_id, target in samples:
   899	        row = output_matrix[row_id]
   900	        score = dot(hidden, row)
   901	        prob = sigmoid(score)
   902	        error = target - prob
   903	        row_before = list(row)
   904	        for i in range(args.dim):
   905	            row[i] += args.lr * error * hidden[i]
   906	        for i in range(args.dim):
   907	            grad_hidden[i] += args.lr * error * row_before[i]
   908	        if target > 0.0:
   909	            loss -= math.log(max(prob, 1e-12))
   910	        else:
   911	            loss -= math.log(max(1.0 - prob, 1e-12))
   912	    apply_input_gradient(input_matrix, features, grad_hidden)
   913	    return loss

   916	def train_unsupervised(args: TrainingArgs) -> Model:
   917	    dictionary, examples = Dictionary.build(args.input, args)
   918	    rng = random.Random(args.seed)
   919	    input_matrix = make_input_matrix(len(dictionary.words), args.bucket, args.dim, rng)
   920	    output_matrix = random_matrix(len(dictionary.words), args.dim, rng)
   921	    maybe_seed_with_pretrained(input_matrix, dictionary, args)
   922	    negative_table = build_negative_table(dictionary.word_counts)
   923	    sentences = [dictionary.sentence_word_ids(example.tokens) for example in examples]
   924	    started_at = time.time()
   925	    total_words = 0
   926	    last_loss = 0.0
   927	    for _epoch in range(max(args.epoch, 1)):
   928	        for sentence in sentences:
   929	            for position, target_id in enumerate(sentence):
   930	                b = rng.randint(1, max(args.ws, 1))
   931	                start = max(0, position - b)
   932	                end = min(len(sentence), position + b + 1)
   933	                if args.model == "cbow":
   934	                    context_features: List[int] = []
   935	                    for ctx in range(start, end):
   936	                        if ctx == position:
   937	                            continue
   938	                        context_features.extend(dictionary.word_feature_cache[sentence[ctx]])
   939	                    if not context_features:
   940	                        continue
   941	                    last_loss = ns_update(args, input_matrix, output_matrix, context_features, target_id, negative_table, rng)
   942	                    total_words += 1
   943	                    continue
   944	                center_features = dictionary.word_feature_cache[target_id]
   945	                for ctx in range(start, end):
   946	                    if ctx == position:
   947	                        continue
   948	                    context_id = sentence[ctx]
   949	                    last_loss = ns_update(args, input_matrix, output_matrix, center_features, context_id, negative_table, rng)
   950	                    total_words += 1
   951	    model = Model(args=args, dictionary=dictionary, input_matrix=input_matrix, output_matrix=output_matrix)
   952	    write_training_progress(args, dictionary, 0, total_words, last_loss, started_at)
   953	    return model

  1016	def command_test(argv: Sequence[str], by_label: bool) -> None:
  1017	    if len(argv) < 2:
  1018	        print_stdout(USAGE_TEST_LABEL if by_label else USAGE_TEST)
  1019	        raise SystemExit(1)
  1020	    model = Model.load(argv[0])
  1021	    data_path = argv[1]
  1022	    k = 1
  1023	    threshold = 0.0

  1025	        k = parse_int(argv[2])
  1026	    if len(argv) >= 4:
  1027	        threshold = parse_float(argv[3])
  1028	    total_examples = 0
  1029	    total_hits = 0
  1030	    total_predicted = 0
  1031	    total_gold = 0
  1032	    per_label_gold = {label: 0 for label in model.dictionary.labels}
  1033	    per_label_pred = {label: 0 for label in model.dictionary.labels}
  1034	    per_label_hit = {label: 0 for label in model.dictionary.labels}
  1035	    for raw_line in iter_test_lines(data_path):
  1036	        example = Dictionary.parse_line(raw_line, model.args.label)
  1037	        gold = [label for label in example.labels if label in model.dictionary.label2id]
  1038	        if not gold:
  1039	            continue
  1040	        total_examples += 1
  1041	        predictions = model.predict(example.tokens, k, threshold)
  1042	        predicted_labels = [label for label, _prob in predictions]
  1043	        gold_set = set(gold)
  1044	        hit = sum(1 for label in predicted_labels if label in gold_set)
  1045	        total_hits += hit
  1046	        total_predicted += len(predicted_labels)
  1047	        total_gold += len(gold)
  1048	        for label in gold:
  1049	            per_label_gold[label] += 1
  1050	        for label in predicted_labels:
  1051	            per_label_pred[label] += 1
  1052	            if label in gold_set:
  1053	                per_label_hit[label] += 1
  1054	    precision = (total_hits / total_predicted) if total_predicted else 0.0
  1055	    recall = (total_hits / total_gold) if total_gold else 0.0
  1056	    if by_label:
  1057	        for label in model.dictionary.labels:
  1058	            gold = per_label_gold[label]
  1059	            pred = per_label_pred[label]
  1060	            hit = per_label_hit[label]
  1061	            if gold == 0 or pred == 0:
  1062	                f1 = "--------"
  1063	                pr = "--------"
  1064	                rc = "--------"
  1065	            else:
  1066	                p = hit / pred
  1067	                r = hit / gold
  1068	                f = 0.0 if (p + r) == 0.0 else (2.0 * p * r / (p + r))
  1069	                f1 = fixed6(f)
  1070	                pr = fixed6(p)
  1071	                rc = fixed6(r)
  1072	            print_stdout(f"F1-Score : {f1}  Precision : {pr}  Recall : {rc}   {label}\n")
  1073	        print_stdout(f"N\t{total_examples}\n")
  1074	        print_stdout(f"P@{k}\t{fixed3(precision)}\n")
  1075	        print_stdout(f"R@{k}\t{fixed3(recall)}\n")
  1076	        return
  1077	    print_stdout(f"N\t{total_examples}\n")
  1078	    print_stdout(f"P@{k}\t{float6(precision)}\n")
  1079	    print_stdout(f"R@{k}\t{float6(recall)}\n")

item.text:
Implemented a standalone reimplementation in [src/fasttext_reimpl.py](/workspace/src/fasttext_reimpl.py:1) and a build/install script in [compile.sh](/workspace/compile.sh:1). `compile.sh` replaces `./executable` with the new implementation and preserves the provided observation binary as `./reference_executable`; the new executable does not shell out to it.

The replacement covers the probed CLI surface: top-level/help text, training arg parsing and failure messages, `supervised`/`skipgram`/`cbow`, `predict`/`predict-prob`, `test`/`test-label`, `print-word-vectors`, `print-sentence-vectors`, `print-ngrams`, `nn`, `analogies`, `dump`, and `quantize`. The core pieces are the fastText-style command dispatcher and help/error handling ([src/fasttext_reimpl.py](/workspace/src/fasttext_reimpl.py:16), [src/fasttext_reimpl.py](/workspace/src/fasttext_reimpl.py:357)), dictionary/ngram feature extraction ([src/fasttext_reimpl.py](/workspace/src/fasttext_reimpl.py:454)), supervised and unsupervised training ([src/fasttext_reimpl.py](/workspace/src/fasttext_reimpl.py:765), [src/fasttext_reimpl.py](/workspace/src/fasttext_reimpl.py:916)), prediction/test utilities ([src/fasttext_reimpl.py](/workspace/src/fasttext_reimpl.py:994)), and lazy bucket-backed model storage so default `-bucket 2000000` runs without allocating dense matrices ([src/fasttext_reimpl.py](/workspace/src/fasttext_reimpl.py:234), [src/fasttext_reimpl.py](/workspace/src/fasttext_reimpl.py:597)).

Verified locally against the reference surface for:
- top-level usage and subcommand help/error cases
- supervised train/predict/test/test-label on toy data
- `print-word-vectors`, `print-sentence-vectors`, `print-ngrams`, `dump`
- unsupervised `skipgram`, `nn`, `analogies`
- `quantize`, including the observed `<256 rows` failure path
- default-bucket training behavior

One material limitation remains: model files are self-consistent within this reimplementation, but they are not binary-format compatible with the original fastText `.bin`/`.ftz` files.
